privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.body: Your documents are yours: kept only if you choose, checked by Sovkora, never sold, never used to train a model. The details, in short sections.

sections.p: Krizaka, a company based in Montréal, publishes Verikora. The person in charge of the protection of personal information (Loi 25) is named at the top of this page, with a direct address.

Your e-mail address and a password hash (to run your account), the date you accepted the terms and this notice, the documents you upload and the results of the checks (to give you the service), and billing information handled by Stripe. We do not sell your information and we do not use your documents to train a model.

Your account, your checks and their reports are in a database in Toronto (Ontario, Canada). A document you choose to keep goes where its information panel says. Today Verikora is a development version: that storage is a development store, in the United States, meant for fictional data. In production, Verikora refuses to keep a document outside Canada; the planned store is in Toronto.

Sovkora, Krizaka's analysis engine, reads a document over HTTPS when you ask for a check. Stripe handles payment. Mailgun sends the confirmation e-mails. DigitalOcean hosts the application and the database in Toronto.

By default a document is not kept: as soon as its check has run, its file and its text are purged, and the report stays, with the file's fingerprint. A document that is never checked is purged after a delay the administration sets, 24 hours by default. If you choose to keep it, it stays until you delete it. What is purged may remain in backups until they rotate.

The documents an applicant uploads are purged after their check, unless the applicant agrees to have them kept until the decision. When closing the file, the manager chooses: purge at the decision (the default), or keep one year after the decision, only for the document types the administration allows to be kept. The result of an applicant check is kept 30 days after the consent.

A purge leaves a signed receipt: what was deleted (the file and its text, by their fingerprints), when, and under which rule (after the check, after the delay, at the decision, one year after the decision, or at the applicant's request). It is written once the store has confirmed the deletion. It holds no name, no address, no file name and no title. It can be checked on the verification page.

Your information is processed outside Québec: the application and the database in Toronto (Ontario); the development store in the United States; Stripe and Mailgun may process it outside Canada; where Sovkora processes a document is not yet stated in our register of transfers. The assessment that section 17 of Law 25 requires before a communication outside Québec is being prepared.

sections.h: No decision by a machine alone
sections.p: A person decides. Verikora decides nothing. A check points out signals and quotes passages of the document; you, or the manager of a file, decide. A report is shown only if every passage it quotes is in the document and it uses no refused verdict word (« fraud », « forged »…). Verikora makes no decision based exclusively on automated processing (section 12.1 of Law 25).

You can access, correct or delete your information, withdraw your consent and download your data by writing to the privacy officer. Deleting a document deletes its file, its text and its results. Closing your account deletes your documents. We keep invoices as the law requires.
If a confidentiality incident presents a risk of serious harm, we notify the Commission d'accès à l'information and the people concerned, as the law requires.
To ask a question, use your rights or have your data removed, write through the contact form of krizaka.com. The person in charge of the protection of personal information answers.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.status: Written in good faith from the law, awaiting review by the lawyer before Verikora opens to the public; the refund policy for a single audit is not final. If in doubt, French prevails.

sections.p: Verikora compares a document you give it (a lease, an invoice, a service contract) with published rules and tells you, point by point, what it found, quoting your document. It is an informative check. It is not a legal opinion and it does not replace a lawyer: only a member of the Barreau du Québec can give legal advice in Québec. A result is never a guarantee that a document is lawful or valid.

You must give a real e-mail address and confirm it. You are responsible for your password. One free audit is included per account; creating several accounts to get more is not allowed and the extra accounts may be closed.

After the free audit, an audit costs the price shown at checkout in Canadian dollars, or you subscribe to the Pro plan. Goods and services tax (GST) and Québec sales tax (QST) are added at checkout and shown on your invoice with Krizaka's registration numbers. Payment is handled by Stripe; Verikora never sees your card number.

Refund policy (draft). You can cancel the Pro plan at any time from the customer portal; the plan then ends at the end of the period already paid. The refund terms of a single audit are not written yet.
Your documents are kept in your account only and are sent to Sovkora, Krizaka's analysis engine, to be checked. See the privacy notice for retention, your rights and how to reach our privacy officer.

sections.h: Intellectual property and your right to use the service
sections.p: Verikora, its software, its sets of verification rules, the layout of its reports, its names, its birds and its marks belong to Technologies Krizaka Inc. or its licensors; these terms assign you none of those rights (Copyright Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-42). For the length of your subscription only, you receive a personal, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable right to use the hosted service; the free audit and single audits give you the same right over the result you obtain. Your documents stay yours: you only authorise us to process them to provide the check. Verikora's source code is published under its own licence, stated in its repository: these terms govern the hosted service, that licence governs the code, and nothing here removes what the licence allows you.

Without a written agreement with Krizaka, you may not: resell, rent, sublicense or offer the hosted service or its reports to third parties as a service, or present it under another brand (white label); use it to build or improve a competing service; extract its content or results by automated means; circumvent an account's limits, the free audit, the billing or the security measures; access another account's data; or decompile or disassemble the parts of the hosted service that are not published, except to the extent the law allows despite this clause. A breach may lead to suspended access, after written notice where the situation allows.

The names and logos of Verikora and Krizaka, and their birds, are marks of Technologies Krizaka Inc. (Trademarks Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. T-13). These terms, like the code licence, grant no right to those marks; their use is governed by the policy published at https://github.com/krizaka/.github/blob/main/TRADEMARKS.md.

We answer for our faults. Verikora provides an informative check: we are not responsible for a decision you make or do not make from a result (signing, refusing or amending a lease, accepting or refusing a tenant), for an inaccurate or incomplete document you give us, or for an interruption of the service that is not our fault. Except for intentional or gross fault, our total liability to you for a single event is limited to the amounts you paid Verikora in the 12 months before the event, and we are not liable for indirect damage (loss of profit, loss of opportunity). None of these limits applies to intentional or gross fault, or to bodily or moral injury (art. 1474 C.c.Q.), or to what a consumer cannot waive (art. 10 of the Consumer Protection Act). They apply to the extent the law allows, notably arts. 1435 to 1437 C.c.Q. on the clauses of a contract of adhesion.

These terms are governed by the laws of Québec and the federal laws that apply there. Subject to what follows, the courts of the judicial district of Montréal alone have jurisdiction. A consumer may always sue in the district where they live and cannot waive that right in advance (art. 3149 C.c.Q.; art. 33 of the Code of Civil Procedure).

These terms are written in French, which is the reference version, as the Charter of the French language requires (art. 55). The English version is a courtesy translation; where they differ, French prevails.

download.title: Download
download.lead: Verikora on your phone and your Mac. Your documents stay on your device; only what a check needs is sent, then erased.

ios.name: iPhone and iPad
ios.body: Scan or pick a document, check it, share the signed report. Testing on TestFlight first.

android.name: Android
android.body: The same checks on your Android phone, installed from a release file while the store listing is prepared.

mac.name: Mac
mac.body: Keep a library in a folder on your Mac, drag documents in from Finder. Your documents never leave the folder.

videos.title: See it work
videos.lead: Short recordings made by our automated tests, on a fictitious demo persona and demo data, in the development build. They are re-recorded on every change, so they show the app as it is today.

web-binder.name: On the web: the binder
web-binder.body: Sign in, then the binder: your collections and the checks to look at, then a collection and its documents.

web-report.name: On the web: the report
web-report.body: A document of the library and its report: every finding cites the line it rests on.

android-documents.name: On Android: the app
android-documents.body: Your collections and the documents in them, then the checks and their batches, on the phone.

mac-library.name: On the Mac: the library
mac-library.body: Your library in a folder on the Mac, and the documents in it.
